newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Hospital patients die in Bulgarian cold spell.
newsitem.headline: Hospital patients die in Bulgarian cold spell.

text.p: Four patients have died at an unheated Bulgarian mental hospital during extreme cold weather in the past two days, BTA news agency said on Friday.
Radnevo hospital's medical director Todor Tolev told BTA two of the four patients had died directly from the cold. The hospital has been without heating for the past 10 days.
One of the victims, a woman, jumped out of a second floor window yelling "I'm dying of cold," BTA said.
Bulgaria's heavily-indebted government lacks funds for welfare spending. A health ministry statement said heating fuel had now been secured for the hospital and an investigation was being launched.
Snowstorms on Thursday left 470 Bulgarian towns and villages without power. The snow chaos was worst in the northeast of the country, where Varna's regional governor declared a state of emergency.
Several towns had no fuel for snow-clearing vehicles.
BTA said a tubercolosis hospital in the village of Radountsi had been unable to receive its bread delivery because roads were blocked.
State radio said strong winds and snow were continuing over most of the country but the snow was less heavy than on Thursday and was forecast to stop on Saturday.
